label: neiso 18 oil agtdaily
definition: neiso 18 (PROBE — partial pass; lever for 2025 CC over-dispatch). Baseline (neiso 17 mystic-cod) + --gas-hub-basis-daily: the daily within-month Algonquin Citygate basis shape (mean-preserving, demand-convex) with dual-fuel switched MWh re-attributed to oil. Targets the 2025 winter oil gap (Jan -330 / Dec -303 GWh in baseline). Result per-class TWh (model / EIA-923 %): CC_REGULAR 52.36 -0.0% / 56.37 -0.4% / 55.98 +5.4% (2023/24/25) vs baseline -0.2/-0.2/+8.7% — pulls 2025 CC down 1.77 TWh toward tolerance, 2023/24 stay in tol (no regression). oil 0.088/0.145/2.124 vs actual 0.39/0.31/0.91: recovers winter oil but OVERSHOOTS 2025 to +134% (the daily-AGT convexity, fitted not forecast-grade, builds too much oil at the 26 $/MMBtu winter spike). CT_PEAKER (-84%) and ST_GAS (-96%) unchanged — this lever does not touch the summer CT/ST wedge. Verdict: most effective single lever on the 2025 CC gap, but needs a damped basis convexity / oil-frac cap to stop the oil overshoot before it is a keeper. | CAMPD triangulation (completeness check on the +8.7% headline): on the same CEMS plant set, model/CAMPD CC = +16.6/+13.8/+19.0% (2023/24/25) and EIA-923/CAMPD = +17.9/+15.0/+9.6%. The 923-over-CAMPD premium is stable ~15-18% in 2023/24 but collapses to +9.6% in 2025 => EIA-923 CC_REGULAR 2025 is itself ~2.5 TWh UNDERCOUNTED (still filling in), not ground truth. Decompose the +8.7% (~4.6 TWh): ~2.5 TWh is 923 incompleteness, ~2 TWh is real over-dispatch (model +19% vs the ~15% CAMPD norm = the within-gas winter-oil/summer-CT-ST split). EIA-930 gas 60.1 ~= model 60.0 confirms the gas envelope is right. Real CC error ~+3-4%, not +8.7%; do not tune to the preliminary 923 bar.
